To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a semantic relatedness metric that is based on the information provided by search engines and that is able to correlate well with human judgment and to help in some tasks of the Semantic Web.

we propose a novel measure of semantic relatedness among words that exploits the information about word frequency provided by existing Web search engines, and that this measure fulfils some desirable properties to be useful in Semantic Web applications.
we have defined a novel, effective, and efficient semantic relatedness measure, that can be used to solve different problems in the Semantic Web.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a measure of semantic relatedness between words and ontology terms that can be applied to different tasks on the Semantic Web.
the development of a novel, effective and scalable measure of semantic relatedness, based on the Web as knowledge base.
the use of the Web to measure the degree in which words and ontology terms are semantically related.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed measure is the first one that is both accurate and scalable for large-scale Semantic Web applications.
the proposed measures are useful in many applications, and that they can be considered as a good alternative to existing measures.
our proposed measure is a promising candidate for the Semantic Web.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a novel, simple and effective measure to compute semantic relatedness, that can be used on the Web and on the Semantic Web.
, given a set of words (or concepts), our measure provides a ranking of the most related ones, which can be used to disambiguate the meaning of a word, or to match concepts in ontologies.
, in this paper, we present a new measure of semantic relatedness among words, and a new measure of relatedness between ontology terms, that uses the knowledge provided by the Web.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, given a set of words, we can estimate the semantic relatedness among them using only the Web as source of knowledge.
the Web is an important knowledge source to be exploited in Semantic Web applications.
the use of Web data is a good source for semantic measures.
